definitions.explanation: Losing a war. In Japanese, this word most commonly refers to Japan's defeat in World War II, but it can also describe any military defeat or, more broadly, losing in a competition or match.

examples.japanese: {敗戦|はいせん}から{日本|にほん}は{立|た}ち{直|なお}った。
examples.english: Japan recovered from its wartime defeat.

examples.japanese: {敗戦|はいせん}の{責任|せきにん}を{問|と}う{声|こえ}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: Voices arose calling for accountability for the defeat.

examples.japanese: {敗戦|はいせん}{直後|ちょくご}の{日本|にほん}は{食料|しょくりょう}も{物資|ぶっし}も{不足|ふそく}し、{多|おお}くの{国民|こくみん}が{苦|くる}しい{生活|せいかつ}を{強|し}いられた。
examples.english: Immediately after the defeat, Japan lacked food and supplies, and many citizens were forced to endure difficult lives.

notes:
USAGE:
When used without further context, {敗戦|はいせん} in Japanese most often refers to Japan's defeat in World War II (1945). The word {終戦|しゅうせん} (end of the war) is a more neutral alternative often used officially, while {敗戦|はいせん} explicitly acknowledges defeat. In sports contexts, {敗戦|はいせん} can also mean a loss or defeat in a game.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {敗戦|はいせん}{後|ご}: after the defeat
- {敗戦|はいせん}{国|こく}: defeated nation
- {敗戦|はいせん}の{色|いろ}が{濃|こ}い: defeat appears imminent (lit. "the color of defeat is thick")

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {終戦|しゅうせん}: end of the war (neutral, avoids the word "defeat")
- {敗北|はいぼく}: defeat (broader; applies to battles, elections, and competitions)
